inputManifest.domain: Source-size bounded encoded sRGB proxy exported by NativeHDRProcessor. No new decode/conversion or model inference.
inputManifest.scope: Twelve consecutive natural source proxy frames1496…1507 for an isolated actual NativeOpticalFlow comparison. Repeated traversals introduce explicitly recorded1507→1496 index discontinuities; timings are not source-rate playback.

design.warmupPolicy: Exclude source indices 1496 through 1498 on every traversal; retained raw data includes them.
design.wrapPolicy: Repeated 1507 to 1496 traversal boundaries are artificial discontinuities, not continuous source-rate playback.
design.timingBoundary: Completed NativeOpticalFlow.prepare wall; array readback, hashing, byte comparisons and memory snapshots occur outside the timer.
design.comparisons: All 144 matched signatures agree: one initial no-motion pair plus 143 vector/confidence SHA256 and scalar-bit/reset comparisons. 24 cut/first-warmed controls also compare full array bytes directly.

statisticsDefinition: Seconds; p95 uses nearest rank ceil(0.95*N), sums use all selected calls. Warmup excludes indices1496..1498 on every traversal.

allCallsCSV.scope: Exact cells from independent samples.csv; only CRLF normalized. Blank comparison cells were not comparison sites, not failures.

resources.alignmentLimit: Host time is sampled before disk/ps and later report read; published count is traversal-granular and can advance during sampling. No exact host-time-to-prepare-call or per-case RSS attribution.

resourceInterpretation: Process-tree RSS includes Swift/XCTest and readback/report storage. MLX counters share one process across both estimators and are not per-strategy independent peaks. The observed peak is the final sampled row after 288 published calls. Byte-summary sum fields sum snapshots; they do not represent cumulative allocation. Watchdogs are operational limits, not acceptance thresholds.

cpuAllocationFeasibility.scope: CPU CoreVideo allocation only: no pixel fill, CoreImage resize, VT optical flow, Metal commands, MLX or model execution. No end-to-end performance or process-memory bound claim.
cpuAllocationFeasibility.summaryRevision: Correct allocation summary metric names from Seconds to Microseconds. Raw probe seconds and original artifacts are unchanged; no measurement rerun.

measurementDesign.allocationTiming: Swift allocator wrapper and CoreVideo call elapsed on monotonic DispatchTime; excludes IOSurface ID/geometry reads, retention release, JSON recording and any pixel fill. Pool construction is separately recorded.
measurementDesign.retention: One old working buffer and one current live through the flow-pair allocations; current becomes next previous, flow pair released at each iteration end. Ownership controls separately retain every hypothesized slot.

attributes.pool: nil: default minimum/maximum age; no preallocation, threshold only in auxAttributes

limitations: No pixel initialization by the probe, CoreImage render, VideoToolbox request, MLX import or GPU work occurs. Lazy surface commitment, zeroing and driver-held ownership under real processing are not measured.

IOSurface IDs can be recycled globally after deallocation: fresh allocations also repeat IDs. Unique IDs alone do not prove persistent object/backing identity. Retained simultaneous leases stay distinct; the pool release/reacquisition control is interpreted together with the allocation-threshold result.

Working threshold3 and flow threshold4 are tested hypotheses and suffice for this sequential CPU retention pattern; they are not proven minimum sizes or safe production maxima under asynchronous consumer retention.
Pools use default age policy and are reconstructed per case/round; no preallocation is hidden. The32 warmup iterations are fully retained in raw timing data.
Short allocation-only rounds share one process and local allocator/system state. Six balanced alternating orders control simple ordering effects; they are not independent end-to-end playback trials.

Runtime/RSS limits are guardrails. Internal peak RSS is sampled before JSON serialization and external RSS is sampled; IOSurface bytes and resident memory accounting do not establish a hard physical-memory bound.
cpuAllocationFeasibility.relationToCandidate: The CPU probe used default pool age-out and no pixel writes/CI/VT/MLX. The actual candidate disabled age-out. Allocation-call savings cannot be transferred to completed motion time.

limitations: Completed NativeOpticalFlow.prepare wall includes input half conversion, CI resize, VT processing, motion import, confidence and reset; no isolated allocation or GPU timing.
No model, rendering, audio, Live throughput or perceptual-quality qualification. These are repeated source traversal diagnostics.
Two persistent estimators each span all four pairs; successive pair/case samples are not independent cold processes.
First three calls per traversal are excluded by policy, not evidence of independently steady thermals or stationarity.
Array readback/hash/direct comparisons occur outside prepare timing but affect cache, resources and operating conditions.
Exact signatures verify stored vector/confidence hashes and scalar bits; only24 controls performed direct full-array byte comparison during the actual run.
Raw forward/backward VT buffers, internal allocator events and physical GPU occupancy are not captured.
CoreVideo reuse/cap controls are separate tests. Timing alone cannot establish allocations saved or recommend retention when paired benefit is inconsistent.
Host RSS and reported MLX counters describe different scopes; operational watchdogs are not memory or performance acceptance thresholds.
The retained 99.038792-ms pooled warmed outlier is included. All four paired warmed means and p95 were higher; individual traversal sums were mixed.
One short process cannot identify why pooled time increased or establish a universal result for CoreVideo pooling.
No inference of full model quality, sustained memory bounds, physical HDR, source-rate Live or M5 performance.
